page: Amazon Web Services m6g.2xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors, utilizing the arm64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz with the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results place the instance in the middle tier for several standard operations. It demonstrates average performance in stress-ng single-core (1519.4) and multi-core (12135.21) tests, as well as in Geekbench multi-core workloads (5355.0) such as software compilation and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth is measured at 472.85 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 120.79 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-threaded performance is a notable tradeoff; the instance scores in the bottom 25% for Geekbench single-core tests (936.0) and shows poor performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression (7.3 GB/sec) and Passmark CPU encryption tests (1083.15).

The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the custom ARM-based architecture offers a resource-dense alternative to traditional x86 platforms for workloads that scale horizontally across dedicated physical cores. Given the balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio and average performance in database operations (5174.5 in Passmark) and Redis SET operations (9.56 million operations per second), the m6g.2xlarge is suited for static web serving, caching layers, database operations, and multi-threaded application servers that do not rely on specialized x86 instruction sets.
